nuggets.title: Turn Latency Exceeds 800ms Voice UX Threshold

scenario.symptoms: Users interrupt the assistant mid-sentence; session abandon rate rises 22%. Traces show 1.4s from end-of-speech to first audio byte due to serial STT, LLM, TTS pipeline.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Pipeline waits for full STT transcript before LLM call; TTS starts only after complete LLM response text.

incident.headline: Serial batch speech pipeline breaks interactive voice latency budget

agenda.goal: Hit sub-800ms turn latency with streaming STT, speculative LLM, and streaming TTS overlap.
agenda.opener: Users say the assistant feels sluggish on the phone. Walk through timing from when they stop talking to when they hear a reply.

evidence.strong: Streaming STT partials, endpointing, LLM on partial with correction, streaming TTS on first tokens, colocate services, measure per-stage budget.
evidence.adequate: Faster model only without pipeline overlap.
evidence.weak: Record entire utterance then batch process.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes only model size determines voice latency.
misconceptions.challenge: How much time is waiting for full transcript vs inference?

agenda.referenceFix: Streaming STT/LLM/TTS with overlapping pipeline and tight per-stage timeouts.

nuggets.title: Assistant Talks Over User During Barge-In

scenario.symptoms: Customers yell 'stop' repeatedly while TTS continues for 3 seconds. Turn-taking state machine ignores VAD during playback.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Half-duplex mode: mic muted while assistant speaks; barge-in events not wired to cancel TTS stream.

incident.headline: Turn manager lacks barge-in handling to stop playback and capture user speech

agenda.goal: Implement full-duplex or fast barge-in with VAD, TTS cancel, and clear speaking/listening states.
agenda.opener: Users can't interrupt the bot while it's talking. How does turn-taking work in your voice agent?

evidence.strong: Full-duplex VAD during TTS, immediate playback cancel, truncate LLM generation, echo cancellation, explicit FSM states, test barge-in latency.

misconceptions.pattern: Treats push-to-talk as sufficient for natural conversation.
misconceptions.challenge: Do real phone support calls allow interruption?

probes: How fast must TTS stop after user speaks?
agenda.referenceFix: Barge-in path cancels TTS within 200ms and pivots to listening state.

nuggets.title: Agent Promises Transfer Without Calling Telephony API

scenario.symptoms: Callers stay on hold indefinitely after assistant says 'connecting you to a specialist'. Logs show no TransferCall tool invocation.
scenario.interviewerSetup: LLM instructed to be helpful can verbalize transfer without forced tool call; no guardrail validates action completion.

incident.headline: Voice agent verbalizes actions without executing required tool calls

agenda.goal: Ground responses in tool results; block claims of actions until tools succeed; safety prompts and classifiers.
agenda.opener: The bot told callers they were transferred but nothing happened. How do you prevent harmful or false voice agent behavior?

evidence.strong: Tool-first patterns for actions, response validation layer, prohibited claim templates, escalation on low confidence, log tool-result pairing.
evidence.adequate: Prompt says don't lie without enforcement.

misconceptions.pattern: Relies on system prompt alone for action honesty.
misconceptions.challenge: Can the model still say 'transferring' without calling Transfer?

hints: Never speak action until tool OK.
agenda.referenceFix: Orchestrator speaks only after TransferCall success; retry or apologize on failure.

nuggets.title: Marketing Spike Exhausts Real-Time Voice Session Pool

scenario.symptoms: New callers hear busy tone during campaign while CPU is only 60%. Session manager limit of 2k concurrent WebRTC legs hit before autoscaler adds nodes.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Hard cap on concurrent sessions per control plane with slow scale-out; no queue with estimated wait callback.

incident.headline: Session limits and slow scale-out reject calls despite available cluster headroom

agenda.goal: Scale real-time voice horizontally with pre-warm capacity, queue/callback, and per-region pools.
agenda.opener: Campaign drove busy signals while servers looked half idle. How many concurrent voice sessions can you handle and how do you scale?

evidence.strong: Horizontal media servers, pre-warm before campaigns, queue with callback offer, regional sharding, limit admission with message not busy tone.

misconceptions.pattern: Uses CPU only to decide capacity.
misconceptions.challenge: What limits concurrent WebRTC sessions besides CPU?

probes: What do callers hear at capacity?
hints: Session counts matter as much as CPU.
agenda.referenceFix: Pre-warmed pool, fast horizontal scale, queued callback UX.

nuggets.title: STT Model Upgrade Hurts Intent Detection in Noise

scenario.symptoms: After STT v3 deploy, misrouted intents rise 18% on car Bluetooth calls. Offline WER improved on clean LibriSpeech but not on telephony noise set.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Release gated on clean speech benchmark only; no eval on production noisy sample or downstream intent accuracy.

incident.headline: STT evaluation on clean speech fails to predict real-world voice agent quality regression

agenda.goal: Evaluate voice stack on noisy telephony samples and end-to-end task success not WER alone.
agenda.opener: WER looked better but callers get misrouted more on car speakers. How do you evaluate speech and agent changes?

evidence.strong: Telephony noise test set, intent accuracy E2E, shadow traffic canary, human review sample, slice by device and accent.
evidence.adequate: WER on internal clean set only.

misconceptions.pattern: Uses academic WER as sole release gate.
misconceptions.challenge: Does lower WER on clean audio imply better intent routing in cars?

agenda.referenceFix: Gate STT releases on noisy set WER and intent accuracy canary.
